guide.callout.body1: Choose what you’re making and describe your goal. Add a script or references if you have them.
guide.callout.body2: Prepare a request, then bring it into your editing chat with your footage or source material.
guide.footnote.lead: A home base for the process.
guide.footnote.rest: The website organizes existing files, previews and saved review decisions. Work starts when you bring your request to the editing chat. Keep using the same project folder in a new chat so the assistant can read its saved status and continue.
guide.hero.lede: The chat is where we create. The studio is where you see the work, find inspiration and pick up the next version.
guide.reference.boundary: The + selects here; it doesn’t send a message. Files stay in this local setup. A copied link opens its saved preview and context while the studio is running; sharing media with someone else needs a separate accessible file or source link.
guide.reference.collection.body: Save a source link with Add reference. The next step is Copy analysis request; paste it into your editing chat. Skip it for now and the prompt stays with the reference. Bring your own finished edits to chat. Each person builds their own library.
guide.reference.collection.title: Your own collection
guide.reference.eyebrow: BORROW THE IDEA. MAKE A NEW EDIT.
guide.reference.mix.body: Use + to select examples, then Review selected references. Save any notes about what you want to borrow. Copy for chat includes each exact example and its saved notes; Preview message is optional.
guide.reference.mix.title: A mix of ideas
guide.reference.one.body: Use the copy icon beside +, or open a reference and choose Copy for chat. Add an optional note and timestamp, Save note, then copy it into your editing chat.
guide.reference.one.title: One reference
guide.reference.title: See something you like?
guide.step1.body: Develop a script from an idea, a draft or a creator reference in your editing chat. Or bring recorded footage and go straight to the spoken cut. Approve the script when it’s ready, record outside the studio, then bring your raw footage to the editing chat.
guide.step1.small: You provide the footage and direction.
guide.step1.title: Start with an idea—or your footage.
guide.step2.body: Your assistant compares takes, removes bad starts and dead air, and joins complete thoughts into a quick, cohesive cut. Watch this version before the graphics work, then approve the spoken cut in the project or in chat.
guide.step2.small: Already edited your speech? Skip this stage and preserve the timing.
guide.step2.title: Get the spoken cut right.
guide.step3.body: Review actual storyboard frames: the on-screen copy, your framing, reference clips, transitions and motion ideas. Give feedback until the direction feels right, then approve the storyboard.
guide.step3.small: Your storyboard stays with the project.
guide.step3.title: See the idea before the edit.
guide.step4.body: Your assistant adds captions, genuine product B-roll, motion graphics, purposeful zooms and transitions, sound effects and audio cleanup. Music is optional and follows your brief.
guide.step4.small: You choose the creative direction; the assistant builds it.
guide.step4.title: Build the full edit.
guide.step5.body: Review the rendered video. Save a note at a video moment or storyboard scene, then ask your editing chat to apply your saved feedback. You can also give feedback directly in chat. New versions sit beside the accepted baseline; earlier reviews stay accessible.
guide.step5.small: Review sound and motion in the rendered video, beyond the still frames.
guide.step5.title: Watch. React. Refine.
guide.step6.body: Use Approve & mark final in the project, or say it is final in chat. That version is saved in the Reference Library. Reuse its overall feel or a specific technique in your next project.
guide.step6.small: New outside references are added when you share them as inspiration.
guide.step6.title: Call it final. Keep the style.

quickstart.docTitle: Make the reference yours · Assaf’s Studio
quickstart.eyebrow: FROM “I LIKE THAT” TO YOUR NEXT EDIT
quickstart.intro: Each person builds their own collection. Add your own videos, carousels and references as you go. Your local videos stay on your computer.
quickstart.lede: Your finished edits. Your favorite creator references. One place to find the next idea.
quickstart.localFiles.body1: Your library links open your installation while it’s running. They don’t upload your files or give someone on another computer access. In a chat working in your studio folder, the assistant can resolve the link’s reference ID and read the saved media and notes—even if the local server needs restarting. Elsewhere, share a usable original source link or upload the media.
quickstart.localFiles.body2: For a technique, the library link remembers the chosen example; for a carousel, copying inside the pane remembers the viewed slide. A library link points to the current registered reference. An original source link can still require sign-in or become unavailable. If your assistant can’t inspect it, it should ask for a usable source.
quickstart.localFiles.body3: Selections and example choices stay in this browser. Saved borrowing notes stay with your studio, tied to the exact source or example. Clearing a selection keeps its saved notes. Earlier browser notes can be reviewed and saved into the studio. Save an agreed creative direction in the project brief so the next chat can pick it up.
quickstart.localFiles.body4: Borrow the idea and adapt it to your brief. An outside reference doesn’t grant permission to reuse its footage or audio.
quickstart.localFiles.title: A quick note about local files.
quickstart.simple.body1: Tap the copy icon beside + on any card. It copies the exact reference and its saved borrowing notes. Your own work and creator examples work the same way.
quickstart.simple.body2: The link opens the saved context and preview when available. You can also choose Copy for chat inside the detail pane. A creator’s original URL is available there as Copy original link.
quickstart.simple.title: Copy the reference.
quickstart.specific.body1: Choose Add a note to name a moment, slide or detail. For techniques, first choose the exact creator example.
quickstart.specific.body2: Write what you want to borrow, optionally use Add timestamp, then Save note. Press Copy for chat to include the saved notes. Preview message is optional when combining references.
quickstart.specific.title: Add a little direction.
quickstart.step1.body: You don’t need a long prompt. One clear sentence helps your assistant focus:
quickstart.step1.pre:
Use the card entrance at 0:02–0:05 as inspiration for my opening. I like how the cards arrive around the creator. Use my footage and the websites in my new script.

[Paste the copied reference link here.]

Start with a storyboard for review.
quickstart.step1.title: Say what caught your eye.
quickstart.step2.body: Want the opening from one video and the captions from another? Press + on each card. Then choose Review selected references, add a note for each and paste the combined references into chat.
quickstart.step2.note: The check mark means “selected here.” It doesn’t send a message or start an edit. You decide what reaches the chat when you copy and paste.
quickstart.step2.title: Mix a few ideas.
quickstart.step3.body: Use Add reference in the library to save a source link. Add a title, creator and what caught your eye if you want. Saving shows Copy analysis request as the next step: copy it and paste it into your editing chat to inspect the source and enrich that same entry. Choose Keep browsing to do it later; the card stays Awaiting analysis until it has actual analysis. Nothing is sent automatically. Find Edit details in Reference options (…).
quickstart.step3.body2: In your studio chat, attach your video or provide its local path. For another creator’s work, supply the original link. Try:
quickstart.step3.body3: Your assistant should check the source, record the creator and useful moments, and update your collection. A reference it can’t access should be labeled honestly. Your collection is your own; it doesn’t require Matt’s videos.
quickstart.step3.pre:
Add this to my reference library. It’s [my finished video / another creator’s reference]. I like [the opening, a transition, the captions…]. Keep it easy to find for future edits.

[Attach the file or paste its path or original link.]

updates.requestText: Update my studio to the newest version of https://github.com/asaf5767/claude-video-studio (the main branch). Work in this studio folder. If it is a git folder, run git pull; if that cannot finish cleanly, stop and tell me, and never reset, clean or delete anything. If it was installed from a ZIP, download https://github.com/asaf5767/claude-video-studio/archive/refs/heads/main.zip and copy its files over this folder without deleting anything, skipping my own data entirely: projects/, references/, models/, bin/, logs/, .env, .claude/ (except .claude/skills/), style-library/settings.json, style-library/catalog.json, style-library/projects.json, style-library/reference-notes.json, style-library/writing-voice.json, style-library/runtime/, style-library/references/, and the posters/, techniques/ and reference-previews/ folders in style-library/dist/assets/. Then follow .claude/skills/setup-studio/SKILL.md quietly to add anything new (ask me before any install) and restart the studio with python style-library/start.py --restart --open. Do not publish or push anything. Tell me in plain words what changed.

fx.zoomthru.name: Zoom through a word
fx.zoomthru.desc: The camera flies into a word and comes out in the next scene.
fx.kinetic.name: Kinetic typography
fx.kinetic.desc: Words swing in with motion blur and a little bounce at the end.
fx.mask.name: Mask reveal
fx.mask.desc: A line stretches out and the title is revealed beneath it.
fx.trim.name: A line that draws itself
fx.trim.desc: Trim path: a line traces a route and words appear along it.
fx.morph.name: Shape morph
fx.morph.desc: A circle stretches into a button, then into a card with text.
fx.particles.name: Particle burst
fx.particles.desc: A word lands and sets off a burst of sparks.
fx.leak.name: Light leak
fx.leak.desc: A warm flash of light sweeps across the screen, a cinematic transition.
fx.flare.name: Lens flare on a title
fx.flare.desc: A bright beam sweeps across the title as it lands.
fx.glitch.name: Glitch transition
fx.glitch.desc: The screen breaks into strips and color channels, then rebuilds as the next scene.
fx.liquid.name: Liquid transition
fx.liquid.desc: A blob of color spreads over the screen, and the next scene starts from there.
fx.spinblur.name: Spin blur
fx.spinblur.desc: The frame spins fast and lands on the next scene.
fx.cascade.name: Word cascade
fx.cascade.desc: An opening line that drops in step by step, word after word.
fx.impact.name: Impact + chromatic aberration
fx.impact.desc: A big moment: a shake, a flash and color channels that slip for a second.
fx.pop.name: Pop-up stickers
fx.pop.desc: Icons and tags pop up around you with a rubbery bounce.
fx.marker.name: Highlighter
fx.marker.desc: A glowing marker sweeps over the key word in the sentence.
fx.explode.name: Letters break apart
fx.explode.desc: A word breaks into letters that fly in every direction.
fx.counter.name: Growing chart
fx.counter.desc: Bars grow and the number on top counts up.
fx.dotwave.name: Dot-wave background
fx.dotwave.desc: A grid of dots moving like a wave, a live background for titles.
look.popout.name: Breaking out of the frame
look.popout.desc: You're inside a window, and your head breaks out over the top.
look.green.name: Green screen, new background
look.green.desc: Your background is swapped for another: a color, a picture or a screen.
look.behind.name: Text behind you
look.behind.desc: A huge title on the wall, and you stand in front of it.
look.sticker.name: Sticker
look.sticker.desc: You as a sticker with a white outline and a shadow, on a colorful background.
look.split.name: Split screen
look.split.desc: Half you, half the screen or demo you're showing.
look.bubble.name: Bubble on screen
look.bubble.desc: A full screen recording, with you in a small circle in the corner.
look.portrait.name: Blurred background
look.portrait.desc: "Portrait mode": the background blurs and you stay sharp.
look.doc.name: Documentary card
look.doc.desc: You in black and white on a colored circle, with a title in bars.
look.spot.name: Spotlight
look.spot.desc: The background goes dark and a soft light falls on you, for a dramatic moment.
look.clones.name: Clones
look.clones.desc: Three of you in the same room, for roles or before/after.
